svg.title: LSM Tree vs B-Tree
svg.desc: LSM Tree vs B-Tree. Two storage engine designs: update pages in place, or append in memory and merge sorted files, and what each costs to read and write. Step 1, B-tree: pages in place: In time order, 50,000 inserts dirty 172 index pages; for random orders they dirty all 4,927 leaves. Step 2, LSM: log, sort, flush: The LSM model appends the 50,000 reviews to a WAL, sorts them in memory and flushes 3 sorted files. Step 3, Reads and compaction: Order 181,236: bloom filters skip 2 files and key ranges 2 levels; 2 files read. Then L0 compacts. Step 4, Write, read, space: B-tree: one root-to-leaf path per read, pages rewritten in place. LSM: cheap writes, more to merge.

g.text: In time order, 50,000 inserts dirty 172 index pages; for random orders they dirty all 4,927 leaves.
The LSM model appends the 50,000 reviews to a WAL, sorts them in memory and flushes 3 sorted files.
Order 181,236: bloom filters skip 2 files and key ranges 2 levels; 2 files read. Then L0 compacts.
B-tree: one root-to-leaf path per read, pages rewritten in place. LSM: cheap writes, more to merge.
INSERT INTO ev SELECT * FROM order_events WHERE id > 1450000 -- next 50,000, time order
CHECKPOINT; INSERT INTO ev SELECT * FROM late_events -- 50,000 reviews, random orders
db.put((order_id, id), event) × 50,000 -- the same reviews, Python LSM model
db.get(181236) -- every event of order 181,236: memtable, L0 newest first, L1 to L3
db.delete((order_id, id)) for the 30,199 events of 9,755 cancelled orders
SELECT * FROM ev WHERE order_id = 181236 -- the same read in the B-tree
LSM tree · simplified model in Python · same events
Each dirtied page is an 8 kB write
at the next checkpoint. Its first
change after a checkpoint also logs
a full-page image in the WAL.
In time order, entries land at the
moving half of leaf 4,771 to page
A flush writes one immutable file,
back. Below L0, each level is one
sorted run cut into 0.6 MB files.
every file that may hold the order
them with L1: 7 files in, 7 out,
only at L3 can they be dropped.
PostgreSQL run vs the LSM model
two of read, update and memory
overhead, and the third has a floor.
